the persistence of partially contrast-enhanced patterns and the number of winners in WTA networks can be controlled by the shape of a sigmoid signal function that depends on AHP currents and ACh.

(1) in recurrent spiking networks, the sigmoid signal function controls the persistence of a pattern in short-term memory, and the number of cells stored, and (2) neuromodulation by ACh changes the sigmoid shape, which changes the dynamics of the network, and thus the number of cells and the persistence of the pattern in STM.

the dynamics of spiking cortical networks that are modulated by AHP currents and neuromodulators.
how recurrent networks of spiking cells can process and store patterns, and how the dynamics of these networks can be modulated by neuromodulators such as ACh.
how recurrent cortical circuits process and store patterns, and how they may be altered by neuromodulatory inputs.
